title: Modular Terraform overlay for controlled outbound flows and private name resolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a reusable Terraform overlay module that codifies secure outbound policies (security groups + NACLs), optional egress proxy hooks, and a private DNS/resolution pattern for Private (VPC) deployments. This module is intended for Redwood's Private product customers and Dedicated clusters that require predictable, auditable egress behavior and private name resolution without leaking metadata or external resolution paths.

Scope:
- Terraform module that composes: security groups (least-privilege defaults), NACL templates for subnet-level restrictions, optional egress-proxy and allowlist inputs, and a private DNS configuration (Route53 / Azure Private DNS pattern) with guarded resolver rules.
- Health checks and a small test harness (terraform plan + terratest snippets) to validate policy drift and post-upgrade connectivity.
- Upgrade strategy: schema-compatible inputs, migration guide for existing customers using older vpc modules, and safe rollout plan (canary apply + drift detection).

Non-goals:
- Replacing cloud-provider VPC creation modules; this overlay assumes an existing VPC/subnet topology managed elsewhere.
- Full network observability platform (we will emit telemetry hooks and tags but not build dashboards in this ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published under registry: redwood/vpc-egress-resolution-overlay v0.1.0
Module has CI checks: terraform fmt, validate, plan; and a terratest that simulates 2 subnets with deny-by-default NACLs and validates outbound resolution through configured resolver rules
Module exposes clear inputs for: allowlist CIDRs, cloud-provider resolver rule IDs, egress-proxy endpoint (optional), security_group_tags, and audit_tags
Upgrade path documented: migration steps, example tf code to replace legacy vpc-egress resources, and rollback instructions
Security review completed and signed off by security team (PR link in comments)
implementation_notes: Design: module is a thin overlay composed of smaller internal modules: sg-least-priv, nacl-deny-default, priv-dns-resolver, and egress-proxy-hook. Keep each submodule idempotent and independently testable.
Terraform versions: support >=1.4 and lock provider versions for aws/azure/gcp where relevant. Use provider meta-arguments for aliasing across accounts/vpcs.
Inputs: prefer explicit allowlist and deny-by-default semantics. Provide helper var 'mode' with values [enforce, audit-only] to allow non-disruptive evaluation during canary upgrades.
Outputs: list of security group IDs, NACL IDs, resolver-rule resource ids, and a single 'egress_policy_summary' string for quick human checks.

Healthchecks: create optional 'post_apply_connectivity' module that spins up ephemeral instances in canary subnets to verify DNS resolution, ICMP to allowed destinations, and HTTP to egress-proxy if configured. Tests should be runnable in CI (using multiplexed cloud accounts or localstack/emulators where possible).
Drift detection: add recommended sentinel or terraform-cloud policy examples and a sample Datadog monitor query to alert on unexpected outbound flows.
baseline_risks: Misconfiguration may block legitimate outbound traffic for customers during initial apply; include 'audit-only' and explicit dry-run guidance.
Cloud-provider edge cases: differences in resolver rule behavior across AWS/Azure/GCP; require provider-specific acceptance tests.
Rolling upgrades across many customer stacks could surface subtle naming collisions for resolver rules; include stable naming conventions and tags.
